To find ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{y}+y{e}^{x}) \\  & =0+y{e}^{x} \\  & =y{e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

 

To find ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{y}+{e}^{x}) \\  & =x{e}^{y}+0 \\  & =x{e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we evaluate ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ and ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ at $(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(1,1) & =1\cdot {e}^{1}=e \\ {g}_{yy}(1,1) & =1\cdot {e}^{1}=e\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
{g}_{xx}(1,1)+{g}_{yy}(1,1)=e+e=2e.
$$
